boot.comment: DECIDED BY instructions:u AND CPU TIME. The whole process: the dynamic loader, PL_initialise and consulting the engine, which is the only honest way to price a boot because a control window opened inside main() starts after the loader has run. The inference pin sees the consult alone, 1,486,934 of a 1.97-billion-instruction process, so it confirms what the engine loaded and nothing about the rest. BANDS, each against the worst measured EXCURSION of a battery minimum from this pin, on a box whose loadavg ran 9 to 30 while other gates were running: instructions 0.1% against 0.0024% (42x headroom), which is the pin that decides a small change; CPU 95% against 78% (1.2x), which at that width catches a change of about 1.95x or more and nothing smaller. A quiet box should re-measure the CPU excursion and tighten this band; the loadavg-9 data for this row supports roughly 15%, which would catch 1.15x. RE-PINNED 2026-08-28 for the ergonomics redesign, both directions and both with a mechanism. Instructions fell 1,974,960,571 to 1,960,486,997, 0.73%, because the doors this case walks stopped threading out-parameters and status codes: mt_open returns the runtime, mt_run returns the cursor, and the value comes back through mt_one_int rather than a step, an answers_atom and an int64_t out-parameter. Inferences rose 1,510,104 to 1,511,580, 1,476 more, and that is the cardinality check: mt_one_int is a claim that the question answered exactly ONCE, so it pulls the second answer to find out, where the old spelling took the first and asked nothing. The check is the feature; mt_first makes no such claim and costs no backtrack. RE-PINNED 2026-08-28, inferences 1,511,580 to 1,511,595, +15, by the branch order of metta_inference_budget_spent/3's cumulative check in engine/metta/control.pl. A clause whose if-then-else holds `true` in the then-branch and a real goal in the else COMPILES for 15 inferences more, which is a load-time cost this case is the only one to see, and it buys one inference less per answer on every bounded cursor in both seats: break-even at fifteen answers. Attributed by a four-variant A/B holding file position constant, which separates the operator from the branch order: `> -> throw ; true` and `=< -> throw ; true` both consult engine/metta.pl for 1,418,538 and `=< -> true ; throw` and `> -> true ; throw` both for 1,418,553; three identical samples each way. instructions and cpu_seconds are NOT re-pinned: neither moved beyond its band, this box ran loadavg 9 while the standing numbers were measured quieter, and replacing a pin that did not move would lose the better measurement and blur what this entry attributes. counter_policy: instructions:u and CPU time, each the minimum of three, DECIDE every row, paired: foreign code retires no inferences, so the engine's counter is blind to this binding's own work and is pinned only as a third reading of what the ENGINE did. Wall clock decides nothing and is not recorded.
cpu_policy: perf task-clock minimum of three, seconds, banded on both sides by each row's own declared percent. It exists to catch what an instruction count cannot see, a change that keeps every instruction and wrecks the time they take, so its band is an order of magnitude looser than the instruction band and is not a precision figure.
instruction_policy: perf instructions:u minimum of three under setarch -R and a built environment, banded on both sides by each row's own declared percent; every per-operation row excludes the engine boot in front of it through perf's control descriptors, and `boot` is the whole process on purpose

measurement.seat_repin_comment: RE-PINNED 2026-08-28 under the seat-aware stamp. The previous numbers were taken in a worktree with no MORK artefacts, so the seat did not load; on a tree that has them it does, and it costs 23,155 inferences at boot and two per space operation because its provider joins the ownership seam every add and match consults. That read as a 1.56% boot regression and a 3.77% space-pair one that no code caused. The stamp carries the loaded seats now, ASKED of the engine rather than modelled, so a pin taken in one seat configuration refuses to compare against another instead of reporting the difference as a move.

measurement_conditions: Measured 2026-08-28 on a 32-core box SHARED with other agents' gates, loadavg 9 to 30 throughout. What that load does to each counter was measured rather than assumed. instructions:u is immune to it: across eighteen batteries the spread of a battery's minimum was 0.00002% to 0.129%, and a probe at loadavg 30 read 0.00%, 0.00% and 0.12% on boot, term-in and space-pair. No time-derived counter is: task-clock spread 38% to 64% in that same probe, and cycles:u, tested on the hypothesis that the noise was turbo frequency scaling, read 43.6%, 42.1% and 38.7% -- so the contention is cache and memory rather than frequency, and there is no counter substitution that rescues the time reading here. THE CPU PINS ARE THEREFORE LOADED-BOX FIGURES AND ALL SIX WANT RE-CONFIRMING ON A QUIET BOX, boot first (95% band, 78% excursion, and the shortest region at 0.13s), then term-in (80%/63%), cursor-step and term-out (75%/61-62%), then space-pair (45%/34%) and error-ball (40%/32%). On a quiet box the loadavg-9 data supports about 15% for every row. The instruction pins mostly need nothing, and two of them needed a wider band: cursor-step and term-in are BIMODAL here, their two modes 0.127% and 0.113% apart, which is wider than the 0.1% they carried and wider than the 0.129% battery-minimum spread this paragraph already recorded. Each now declares 0.15% beside the measurement; the other four held at 0.1% through every load level seen here [measured 2026-08-29]. HOW THE PINS WERE TAKEN: min-of-FIFTEEN for the pin, min-of-three for each comparison. The minimum converges on the uncontended value, and fifteen samples land within 5% of the lowest reading ever seen for every case where three samples do not; re-pin with `sh bench.sh --update --rounds 15`. WHERE THEY WERE TAKEN: from extensions/cmetta, which bench.py chdirs to before measuring anything. posix_spawn gives the child the caller's working directory and the engine's boot count moves with it -- 1,973,077,636 from /tmp, 1,974,705,233 from the repository root, 1,975,121,930 from the seat, a 0.104% span wider than boot's own 0.1% band -- so without that anchor a developer and the gate would disagree by more than a regression has to be to fail.
